Use cases/Equity

Spot equity refresh gaps

See who's about to hit a vesting cliff and what a refresh would cost.

For
Comp team, Finance
Uses
Market Data Pro, Total Rewards

The prompt

Ask Pave Agent

Which employees have less than 25 percent of their unvested equity value left over the next 12 months? Compare their ongoing equity to market refresh benchmarks and estimate the cost of bringing them to the 50th percentile.

Then try

  • Break that down by department.
  • What if we only refresh people rated "meets" or higher?

What you get back

Pave Agent

Sample output with illustrative data

38 employees hit a vesting cliff in the next year. Their ongoing equity sits at the 22nd percentile of market refresh grants. Bringing them to the 50th costs about 0.4 percent of fully diluted shares.

Department Employees Ongoing equity position Refresh cost
Engineering 19 24th $2.1M
Product 8 18th $0.9M
Go-to-market 11 26th $0.7M

SourcesEquity grantsHRISMarket Data

The problem

Initial grants are running out for your longest-tenured people. Their pay drops when vesting ends, and that's when they start taking recruiter calls.

The old way

  1. Pull vesting schedules from the cap table tool
  2. Compare to refresh benchmarks by hand
  3. Estimate share cost in a separate model

Why it works in Pave

Reads vesting, not just grants

It looks at what's left to vest, which is what actually drives retention.

Refresh benchmarks

Compares ongoing grants to ongoing grants, not to new-hire packages.

Ties to Total Rewards

The same numbers show up in the employee's total rewards view.

Data it uses

Your data

  • Equity grantsGrants and vesting schedules
  • Share valueCurrent price or 409A
  • Employee job and levelFrom your HRIS

Pave intelligence

  • Equity refresh benchmarksOngoing grant value by level
  • Market Data benchmarksNew-hire equity by company stage

What you need

  • Market Data Pro
  • Total Rewards
